conversation.Statement: Thank you for contacting the Federal Tax Refund Assistance Center. My name is Officer Jonathan Miller with the IRS claims department. How may I assist you today?
Hi, I got a voicemail saying I might be eligible for a tax refund, but I'm not sure what this is about.

Certainly, I can help clarify. As part of the recent IRS stimulus review, our system flagged your taxpayer identification as eligible for a substantial refund. May I verify your full name and date of birth to access your tax file?
Sure, it's Emily Carter, and my birthday is April 6, 2002.

Thank you, Ms. Carter. I now have your file. According to IRS Form 8888, you are entitled to a federal tax refund of $1,942.16. However, your account is pending due to incomplete identity clearance. To comply with IRS anti-fraud protocols, a one-time identity verification fee must be processed before funds can be released.
Oh, I didn't know there was a verification fee. Is that normal? I've never gotten a refund before.

It is standard IRS procedure for first-time refund recipients flagged for manual review. The $98.50 verification fee is fully refundable and ensures your refund is not delayed or revoked under Section 7204 of the IRS code.
Okay, I guess. How do I pay the fee?

For your security, the IRS has partnered with certified payment networks. You may remit the fee by debit card, Zelle transfer, or by purchasing certified government prepaid cards at any major retailer. Which option is most convenient for you?
I only have a debit card, or I guess I could buy a prepaid card. What do most people do?

Most applicants use prepaid cards for rapid processing. If you choose this route, please visit your nearest pharmacy or supermarket and purchase two Vanilla Visa cards totaling $100. Once you have the cards, call me back and provide the codes so I can process your clearance.
So I just buy them and read you the numbers?
Precisely. This ensures your identity verification is logged in our secure IRS system and your refund is released within 24 hours.
What happens if I can't do this today?

Failure to complete the verification by close of business will result in your refund being withheld, and your taxpayer account may be marked for further review. Repeated noncompliance can trigger an IRS audit or financial penalties as per Section 6651.
Wait, I don't want to be audited. Can I just give you my debit card details now?
If you prefer, I can process the fee using your debit card. Please provide the card number, expiration date, and the three-digit code from the back of the card.
Okay, hold on a second. My card number is 5643 7821 9902 1178, it expires 05/27, and the code is 409.
Thank you. I am processing your payment now. Do not disconnect the call. If there are insufficient funds or a processing error, your refund could be delayed and additional IRS action may follow.
It should go through. I have enough, I think.
Excellent. Please confirm your billing address associated with the card for our records.
It's 1445 East Maple Road, Springfield, IL 62704.

Thank you, Ms. Carter. Your payment is being verified. If, for any reason, this transaction is not approved, the IRS will have to initiate a formal notice of tax refund denial, which may negatively impact your standing with federal authorities.
Oh, I really hope that doesn't happen.
If I encounter any issues with this card, I will require you to obtain the prepaid cards or initiate a wire transfer to our authorized IRS processing account to avoid further escalation.
Alright, let me know if you need me to do anything else.

Please remain on standby for the next ten minutes. Should your payment not process, I will instruct you on how to resolve the matter immediately to prevent risk of refund cancellation or additional IRS scrutiny.
